title: Fast-Boot SDK Probe Lab — sprint notes and quickstart experiment plan
content:
Purpose
-----
Notes and lightweight plan for a short, focused 'probe lab' to validate the fastest possible first-run SDK experience across JS/Python/CLI for new users. This is intentionally experimental: small scope, measurable outputs, lightweight deliverables (single-page quickstarts and 2 tiny sample apps).

Background / why this now
-----------------------
- Multiple reports from onboarding funnel: users drop at first API key step or after first error.
- We want a minimal path that guarantees a working 'hello world' within 90 seconds for a new dev.
- Existing docs are thorough but wide; we need a 1-flow path that we can A/B test and later fold into main quickstart if successful.

Goals / Hypotheses
------------------
H1: A single-file example + one CLI command + default environment variable is sufficient for >65% success in first attempt for new users.
H2: A one-click auth token copy + profanity-safe default model will reduce early errors by 40%.
H3: JS quickstart has higher engagement than Python for web dev persona; CLI quickstart is preferred for infra/platform persona.

Success metrics (probe lab week sprint)
-------------------------------------
- Internal usability test: 10 external devs (non-Redwood) complete quickstart in <= 90s: target 7/10.
- Error surface: proportion of test users who hit a credential or permissions error. Target: <20%.
- Telemetry spike: measure first-call latency across SDKs; capture median cold-start token time.
- Qualitative: clarity rating >= 4/5 on 1-page quickstart.

Experiment matrix (short list)
-----------------------------
Variations to try in parallel during the probe week:
- Auth: copy-token (button) vs paste env var method vs ephemeral session link.
- SDK bindings: JS minimal (fetch wrapper) vs official SDK with one-liner import.
- Sample app scope: Console hello-world (chat bubble) vs CLI echo generator.
- Model: safe-small (fp16 quant) vs full sampler (larger) to measure perf tradeoffs.

Quickstart microflow (the 90s path)
----------------------------------
1) Create free account (precondition for the probe test).
2) Click "Copy API key" from onboarding modal. Button copies token to clipboard and offers a single-line CLI command (see A).
3) Paste or accept ephemeral env var.
4) Run one command: it prints a generated sentence.

A. CLI one-liner (example)
- mac/linux: curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small-safety","prompt":"Say hello to Redwood world"}'
- Ideally we replace curl with a tiny CLI shim we ship in npm/pip: `npx redwood-cli hello` (returns sample text).

B. JS single-file (index.js) idea
- One file, no build: 
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small-safety', prompt: 'hello' }) });
console.log(await res.text());

C. Python single-file (hello.py) idea
- `python -c "import os,requests; print(requests.post('https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':f\"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY')}\", 'Content-Type':'application/json'}, json={'model':'redwood-small-safety','prompt':'hello'}).text)"`

Minimum deliverables (end of probe week)
---------------------------------------
- 1-page quickstart for CLI, JS, Python (single-file) that fits in onboarding modal.
- A tiny npm package `@redwood/boot-probe` with one command stub for tests. (Alpha.)
- Usability test notes and telemetry summary doc (spreadsheet).
- Short README for engineering: what we measured and recommended next steps.

Instrumentation & telemetry to capture
------------------------------------
- First-call success/failure (status code + error tags).
- Time from onboarding page open -> first successful response (ms).
- SDK runtime errors: network, auth, parse.
- Model response size and latency.
- Capture anonymized console logs from test users (consent in usability testing).

Acceptance gating for merging into main quickstart
------------------------------------------------
- >= 70% success in lab usability (not counting deliberate adversarial steps).
- No systemic security risk in one-liner approach (review by security team).
- Telemetry shows acceptable latency on default model (median < 400ms for small model in our region).

Open questions / risks (notes to self)
------------------------------------
- Auth UX: clipboard copy is easy but leads to insecure copying in corp environments. Need alternative for enterprise flows.
- Ephemeral session links may be blocked by CS/Legal for audit; check with compliance.
- Which model to choose as default? Safety + latency tradeoffs.
- Should we pre-insert a guardrail prompt for hallucination-sensitive customers? Maybe just call it out.
- Internationalization: examples in English only — consider Spanish quickpass in a follow-up sprint.

Operational checklist for the sprint
----------------------------------
- [ ] Create private branch with single-file quickstarts and tiny CLI stub (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks (owner: Diego).
- [ ] Schedule 2 x 45min remote usability sessions with external devs (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Security review slot requested (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Create spreadsheet to capture time-to-success and error types (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Draft one-page modal copy for onboarding (owner: design lead, @sara).

Post-probe deliverables (if successful)
--------------------------------------
- PR to fold 1-page quickstart into onboarding modal and docs landing.
- Publish `@redwood/boot-probe` as alpha with minimal telemetry opt-in.
- Follow-up experiments: multi-language quickstart, ephemeral session flow, onboarding for platform teams.

Meeting notes (11/05 sprint kickoff)
-----------------------------------
- Priya: keep examples minimal; avoid heavy SDK imports. Agreed.
- Diego: parallel telemetry work needs a small flag in SDK to mark probe traffic.
- Liam: security wants to see token lifetime recommendations if we expose ephemeral options.
- Action: Maya to draft the one-page and share before EOD 11/06.

Quick usability script (10–12min) for lab testing
------------------------------------------------
1) Read intro: "We want you to get a working sample in under 90s. We'll ask you to follow the modal and run the single command. We will time you and ask about pain points after."
2) Give participant a brand-new email-based test account.
3) Observe clipboard use, permission prompts, network issues.
4) After success/failure, ask 3 quick questions: What broke? What would have helped? How likely would you recommend this quickstart?

Notes on drafting the modal copy (1 page)
----------------------------------------
- Keep it action-first. No concepts. Example: Step 1: Click Copy Key. Step 2: Paste into terminal: `export REDWOOD_KEY=...` Step 3: Run: `npx redwood-cli hello`
- Add a tiny troubleshooting line: "If you see 401, check your key or click 'Regenerate' in the console."

Next steps (11/06–11/12)
-----------------------
- Maya: produce 3 one-file quickstarts and CLI stub (11/09).
- Diego: telemetry sketch + small flag in SDK (11/09).
- Priya: recruit 10 external devs and run sessions by 11/12.
- Liam: open security review ticket and confirm token guidance by 11/12.

Misc notes and links
-------------------
- Related PR for small CLI shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842
- Tracking ticket: ENG-2345
